title: Matryoshkas
statementMd:
Matryoshkas are traditional Russian wooden dolls that nest inside one another. Mathias has found a box full of them and wants to put together an exhibition!

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c830c79634ec601ca7a4facb94d6635af5d43da6.png)

The box contains 𝑛n separate dolls. Doll 𝑗j has size 𝑎𝑗aj, an integer between 11 and 𝑛n. Several dolls may have the same size.

To assemble a set of size 𝑖i, Mathias must choose exactly one doll of each size 1,2,…,𝑖1,2,…,i and nest them from smallest to largest. Such a set uses 𝑖i dolls, and its outermost doll has size 𝑖i. A single doll of size 11 also forms a valid set.

To make the exhibition varied, Mathias wants all the sets to have distinct sizes. Each doll may belong to at most one set, and he does not have to use every doll in the box.

What is the largest number of sets he can assemble?

## Input

The first line contains an integer 𝑡t (1≤𝑡≤1051≤t≤105), the number of test cases.

For each test case, the first line contains an integer 𝑛n (1≤𝑛≤1051≤n≤105), the number of dolls. The second line contains 𝑛n integers 𝑎1,𝑎2,…,𝑎𝑛a1,a2,…,an (1≤𝑎𝑗≤𝑛1≤aj≤n), their sizes.

The sum of 𝑛n over all test cases does not exceed 105105.

## Output

For each test case, print a single integer on a separate line: the maximum number of sets of distinct sizes that can be assembled.

## Note

In the second test case, sets of sizes 11 and 22 can be assembled, leaving the doll of size 33 unused. In the fourth test case, only one set of size 11 can be assembled, since all set sizes must be distinct. In the fifth test case, sets of sizes 11, 22, and 33 use all the dolls.
